account: On 21 February 2023 Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud's Constitution Bench heard the Maharashtra political crisis matter in Court Room 1. It used AI live transcription supplied by TERES, with screens facing the lawyers showing the text. The Chief Justice called it an experiment. He said transcripts would go to lawyers for verification and then onto the Supreme Court website (LiveLaw, 21 February 2023). The Supreme Court Observer reported on 18 May 2023 that 25 Constitution Bench hearings had been held across four cases. Only nine transcripts had been published: six for the marriage-equality case, three for the Maharashtra case, none for the other two. None was published in March 2023. NDTV reported on 8 December 2023 a written reply in the Lok Sabha by Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal. He said AI transcription had been deployed for Constitution Bench matters since February. Transcripts in almost ten main matters had been generated and published on the court's website. The use was on a trial basis. A Press Information Bureau feature of 11 February 2026 states that the system is being extended to regular hearing days. That follows successful use in Constitution Bench proceedings.

ai_role.statement: The AI produced the live draft. Lawyers proofread before publication and, per the Chief Justice, people oversee overlapping speech. The published-transcript rate (36% of hearings by May 2023) shows the benefit depended as much on human vetting as on the recognizer.

fields.account: On 21 February 2023 Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud's Constitution Bench heard the Maharashtra political crisis matter in Court Room 1. It used AI live transcription supplied by TERES, with screens facing the lawyers showing the text. The Chief Justice called it an experiment. He said transcripts would go to lawyers for verification and then onto the Supreme Court website (LiveLaw, 21 February 2023). The Supreme Court Observer reported on 18 May 2023 that 25 Constitution Bench hearings had been held across four cases. Only nine transcripts had been published: six for the marriage-equality case, three for the Maharashtra case, none for the other two. None was published in March 2023. NDTV reported on 8 December 2023 a written reply in the Lok Sabha by Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal. He said AI transcription had been deployed for Constitution Bench matters since February. Transcripts in almost ten main matters had been generated and published on the court's website. The use was on a trial basis. A Press Information Bureau feature of 11 February 2026 states that the system is being extended to regular hearing days. That follows successful use in Constitution Bench proceedings.
